name: The heart, blood vessels and blood

terms.definition: Blood passes through the heart twice in each circuit: the right side pumps it to the lungs, the left side to the rest of the body.
terms.examiner: The left ventricle has a thicker wall because it pumps blood all round the body.

terms.definition: A group of cells in the right atrium that controls the natural resting heart rate.
terms.examiner: An artificial pacemaker is an electrical device that corrects an irregular heart rate.

terms.definition: Carries blood away from the heart at high pressure; thick muscular and elastic walls.
terms.examiner: Arteries carry blood away; veins carry it back.

terms.definition: Carries blood back to the heart at low pressure; thinner walls, a wide lumen and valves to stop backflow.
terms.examiner: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood.

terms.definition: A tiny vessel with walls one cell thick, so substances diffuse quickly between the blood and the tissues.
terms.examiner: Link "one cell thick" to "short diffusion distance".

terms.definition: The pale yellow liquid part of blood, carrying cells, glucose, carbon dioxide, urea, hormones and proteins.
terms.examiner: Red blood cells are not part of the plasma.

terms.definition: Carries oxygen: contains haemoglobin, has no nucleus and is a biconcave disc for a large surface area.
terms.examiner: Haemoglobin binds oxygen in the lungs to form oxyhaemoglobin.

terms.definition: A fragment of a cell that helps blood to clot at a wound.
terms.examiner: Clotting stops blood loss and keeps microorganisms out.
